title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is one ternary counter: every bounce of the head adds one, the rule of a bounce is proved in Lean for any number of carry digits, and each digit loses 2 blocks per 9 of its counts, so digits run out and the counter collapses. An exact accelerator follows the run through the collapses forecast in November, to about 10100 steps, and the region-memo accelerator to 3.88×10196 steps, without a halt. Whether some collapse can reach the halting transition is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 99,142 cells have been visited and 42,433 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.489). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062).

claims.title: 11 shift rules
claims.text: For every n, the head crosses n copies of a short word in a fixed number of steps per copy and leaves another word behind (for example the head going left over 0111 and leaving 0100, 18 steps a copy; these cross the 111-blocks of the counter). Generated and proved by bbtools.symtm, checked by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>19</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, crossing long runs of equal blocks in one go; it agrees with the direct simulator at 2×10<sup>9</sup> steps) runs 10,000,000,000,378,843,465 steps without a halt, through the collapses at about 3×10<sup>17</sup>.

claims.title: The draining law
claims.text: Between collapses, the segment j places from the growing end loses 2·3<sup>j</sup> blocks per cycle (6, 18, 54, 162, … per sampled cycle of the macro run), with occasional off-by-one irregularities at the junk near the ends. It is checked on the cycles of the direct run to 4.5×10<sup>9</sup> steps (failing exactly at the collapses) and on the macro run to 10<sup>19</sup>; the far-end rule that makes new segments is not pinned down.

claims.title: The next collapse
claims.text: At 10<sup>19</sup> steps the three segments next to the growing end hold 22,849, 4,261 and 3,351 blocks; the 4,261 runs out first, after about 240 more cycles; cycles have been getting longer by a factor of about 2 on average, so that is far beyond reach.

claims.title: Right-end events to 10<sup>13</sup> steps (16 November 2026)
claims.text: The record-printing macro simulator lists the right-end D events of this machine to 10<sup>13</sup> steps without a halt; no new law was derived, and the bound stays at 10<sup>19</sup> steps.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.88×10<sup>196</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran with blocks of 4 cells, from blank tape for 1200 seconds and reached step 3.88×10196 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 47 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: The counter sweep, for every number of carry digits
claims.text: sweepZ and sweepO: from a sample, any list of T digits and a Z or O stop digit, the machine reaches the next sample with the T digits turned into Z digits (same runs), the stop raised by one, the run changes of the counter rule, in 10 per block of the chain and of the last run, 28 per chain digit, plus 42 steps. Six pieces proved by bbtools.symtm, joined by induction over the list (24 November 2026).

claims.title: The digit model is exact on the direct run
claims.text: Every sample (a new cell at the bouncing end in state D, or B in the mirror) of the direct run to 3×10<sup>7</sup> steps equals the model: 3,851 sweeps (1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD) and 4,049 (1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB), no mismatch.

claims.title: The accelerator is exact
claims.text: Every closed-form counter jump and cycle jump of py/oacc.py equals plain sweeps (11,513 and 4,945 over 6×106 sweeps); accelerated states equal the direct run cell for cell at 1.13×1011 steps (1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD) and at 9.7×109 and 3.2×1010 steps (1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB).

claims.title: Through the forecast collapses, to about 10<sup>100</sup> steps
claims.text: The run of 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB passes its top digit running out at 1.1×10<sup>32</sup> steps; the run of 1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD passes the merge of its top digits at 6.0×10<sup>65</sup> steps; both go on to about 10<sup>100</sup> steps (103 to 104 digits) without a halt (24 November 2026).

claims.title: The next collapses
claims.text: 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB: the third digit (10,607 blocks at 1.76×10<sup>100</sup>, 162 fewer per power of 10) runs out near 10<sup>165</sup>. 1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD: the top digit (11,054 blocks at 1.43×10<sup>101</sup>, about 24 fewer per power of 10) near 10<sup>560</sup>. Fits of the drain, not proofs.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs the head in state D on a 1 with a 1 to its right (D1 → 0RE, E1 halts); inside the draining regime this does not occur, and what a collapse does in general is not known.

The same table as 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is one ternary counter, like an odometer: every bounce of the head adds one, and each digit pays 2 blocks for every 9 times it counts, so the digits drain away and the tape collapses when one runs out. It has survived every collapse seen so far.

facts.text: No halt in an accelerated simulation, through every collapse met.
One bounce of the counter, proved in Lean for every number of carry digits.
The collapse forecast in November, followed exactly: no halt.

sections.heading: One ternary counter at the bouncing end
html: Between visits to its slow end, the head bounces at the other end of the tape, and every bounce adds one to a ternary counter written there. Read from the far end, the tape is a list of digits [r]W: a run of r blocks 1000 and a wall, 101010 for 0, 10 for 1, 100000 for 2, then the last run and 100 next to the head.

the carry stops onwhat changes
a 1 (wall 10)it becomes a 2; its own run loses one block
a 0 (wall 101010)it becomes a 1; the digit below gains one block
alwaysthe 2s below the stop become 0s, the last run gains one block, and the bounce costs 10 steps per block of the carry and of the last run, 28 per carry digit, plus 42

So a digit loses one block every 3 of its own increments and gets one back every 9: two blocks lost per 9 counts. The digits near the far end count least often and last longest; one that runs out makes the neighbours merge (a collapse). The rule is proved in Lean for every number of carry digits, and an exact accelerator built on it went through the collapses that were due, at 1.1×1032 steps (the mirror image) and 6.0×1065 steps (this machine), without a halt.

sections.heading: A list of counters that drain
html: Each time the head writes a new cell at the right end, the tape, read as lengths of runs of 1s from the far end, is 6 3^x1 9 3^x2 9 … 9 3^xm and a little junk: blocks 111 grouped into segments by markers of nine 1s. The numbers xi of blocks per segment are the state. The head sweeps over all of it, so the tape grows like the square root of the time on the far side and very slowly at the growing end.

Its mirror image 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB is this machine started in state E, with left and right swapped and the states relabelled (A→E, B→D, C→A, D→B, E→C); the two runs follow the same law with different numbers.

sections.heading: Faster drains near the end
html: From one cycle to the next the segment next to the growing end loses 6 blocks, the one before it 18, then 54, 162, … (2·3j), like the wheels of an odometer turned backwards. New, very long segments appear at the far end. When a segment near the end runs out the last segments merge and the count starts again: a collapse. The segments next to the growing end in the accelerated run (from the growing end):

The jump in the table is a collapse: the two small segments vanish and the next ones take their place. The next one is far away: the 4,261 runs out first, after about 240 more cycles; cycles have been getting longer by a factor of about 2 on average, so that is far beyond reach.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.489). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062).
After 109 steps the tape spans 99,142 cells (69,451 left of the start, 149 right), with a density of 1s of 0.428.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→B, E→A, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RF_1LC1RF_1RA0LD_0LC0RE_1LD---_0RC0RD: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F; it is this table started in state B

summary: One ternary counter at the bouncing end (rule proved in Lean for any carry); each digit loses 2 blocks per 9 counts, so digits run out and collapse; exact runs pass the forecast collapses (6.0×10<sup>65</sup>) and no halt is known to 3.88×10<sup>196</sup> steps.
family: Nested ternary counter (segments drained at rates 2*3^j, mirrored pair)
